title: Large-Scale Counterfeit Chocolate Production Halted in Vladimir Region
h1: Large-Scale Counterfeit Chocolate Production Halted in Vladimir Region
metaTitle: Large-Scale Counterfeit Chocolate Production Halted in Vladimir Region

excerpt: February 17, 2026 — Law enforcement officers, in cooperation with specialists from Vlasta-Consulting, conducted a large-scale operation to shut down illegal production of chocolate spreads and candies packaged under the guise of…
body: February 17, 2026 — Law enforcement officers, in cooperation with specialists from Vlasta-Consulting, conducted a large-scale operation to shut down illegal production of chocolate spreads and candies packaged under the guise of well-known brands. The raid was the culmination of a multi-stage investigation that had been ongoing since 2023.
Operation details to suppress illegal production:
As part of an initiated criminal case, searches were carried out simultaneously at three locations in one of the districts of the Vladimir region:

• Production workshop. The premises contained industrial mixers, an oven, and loading equipment. Raw materials were stored nearby: containers with liquids, blocks of chocolate mass, coconut flakes, nuts, and vegetable oils. The packaging process was semi-manual.

• Storage location for labels and packaging. Tens of thousands of labels with trademarks confusingly similar to registered brands such as Mars, Snickers, Twix, M&M's, and Bounty were discovered, along with packaging ready for labeling. About 10 citizens working without official registration were present at the site and were detained.
• Warehouse premises. More than 40 unmarked plastic containers filled with chocolate paste were seized, as well as various confectionery products (marmalade, bulk candies).
During the raid, law enforcement seized:
• Technological equipment (mixers, oven, loader, scales);
• Raw materials and production components;
• Labels bearing signs of counterfeiting (totaling over 10,000 units);
• Finished products ready for sale and empty containers not yet labeled.

The organizers and members of the group have been identified. A criminal case has been initiated against the involved individuals under Part 3 of Article 180 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (illegal use of a trademark). Additionally, Article 238 of the Criminal Code (production and sale of products not meeting safety requirements) is being considered, as numerous violations of sanitary standards were recorded at the production site.

The work carried out by law enforcement agencies during this raid deserves high praise: the coordinated actions and professionalism of the officers made it possible to shut down the illegal workshop, thereby protecting both the rights of copyright holders and the health of consumers.

Vlasta-Consulting expresses its readiness to continue providing comprehensive support to law enforcement in conducting such operations aimed at combating counterfeiting and protecting the legal market.
subtitle: Law enforcement officers, in cooperation with specialists from Vlasta-Consulting, conducted a large-scale operation to shut down illegal production of chocolate spreads and candies packaged under the guise of well-known brands.

body: On November 25-26, 2025, the XXXVIII International Scientific and Practical Conference of the Association of Russian Detectives (ARD), titled "Detective – Yesterday, Today, Tomorrow," was held in Moscow. Alexey Solomanidin, an Executive director of Vlasta-Consulting, participated in this significant event for the professional community.

During the ceremonial part of the conference, Alexey Solomanidin, in his capacity as former President of the World Association of Detectives, presented the prestigious "Vinson-Holmes 'Best Security Specialist of the Year' Award" to Alexey Shcherbenev, President of the Association of Russian Detectives. This act of recognition underscored the authority of the Russian detective community on the international stage and Alexey Shcherbenev's significant contribution to the development of the profession.

The conference brought together over 40 delegates from various regions of Russia, as well as partners from Israel, Armenia, and Kyrgyzstan. The participants focused on analyzing the state of the detective movement, current challenges in the legislative regulation of private investigative activities in the Russian Federation, and defining prospects for the profession's development.

The recently adopted Federal Law amending the regulation of private detective and security activities was discussed in detail during the event. Conference participants, including Alexey Solomanidin, noted that the new law requires further refinement, and the detective community faces active work in preparing specific amendments before it comes into force in September 2026.

A particular highlight of the seminars and practical sessions was the topic of implementing innovative technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and competitive intelligence, into the daily practice of private detectives. As participants emphasized, these tools are powerful means of information support, but their results always require thorough professional verification.
Following the conference, a resolution was adopted containing a number of important decisions and recommendations:
• The active use by ARD members of experience in implementing AI and competitive intelligence was initiated.
• The necessity for the continuous improvement of professional competencies among private investigators was emphasized.
• A decision was made to create a working group to develop amendments to the ARD Charter and other documents to enhance the organization's effectiveness.
• The task of intensifying efforts to attract new members and strengthen the association's reputation was outlined.
• The conference organizers were instructed to submit a proposal to the State Duma Committee on Security to involve community experts in finalizing the law on private investigation.

Participation in such an authoritative conference, including the award ceremony, allowed Alexey Solomanidin not only to stay abreast of key trends and legislative changes in the field of private investigation but also to highlight the continuity of professional traditions, exchange experiences with leading industry experts, and strengthen professional connections. The insights and contacts gained will be used for the further development of Vlasta-Consulting's services and to provide the company's clients with solutions that meet the most modern standards and technologies in detective and consulting activities.

title: Vlasta-Consulting Proposes Key Initiative at Anti-Counterfeit Forum
h1: Vlasta-Consulting Proposes Key Initiative at Anti-Counterfeit Forum
metaTitle: Vlasta-Consulting Proposes Key Initiative at Anti-Counterfeit Forum
metaDesc: Representatives of Vlasta-Consulting played a key role in the "Anti-Counterfeit" Forum, proposing an initiative aimed at a systemic solution to the problem of cross-border traffick
excerpt: Representatives of Vlasta-Consulting played a key role in the "Anti-Counterfeit" Forum, proposing an initiative aimed at a systemic solution to the problem of cross-border trafficking of counterfeit products in the countries of the…
body: Representatives of Vlasta-Consulting played a key role in the "Anti-Counterfeit" Forum, proposing an initiative aimed at a systemic solution to the problem of cross-border trafficking of counterfeit products in the countries of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU).

The company participated as a speaker in the first discussion session, "Intellectual Order. Practice of Rights Holders Protection in the EAEU." During his speech, Konstantin Shestera, Operational Director of Vlasta-Consulting, clearly demonstrated the legal gap hindering the effective fight against the illegal market.

He noted that in its practice, the company encounters a situation where a significant amount of information it gathers about the channels of movement and production of counterfeit goods cannot be promptly transferred to the competent authorities. This is due to existing legal and institutional barriers.

"We have encountered a situation where we have nowhere to take the volume of information we can obtain and are willing to share with the authorities," stated Konstantin Shestera. "In the case of the EEC [Eurasian Economic Commission], it is more of a strategic matter, and they cannot guarantee operational efficiency. And in the case of the FTS [Federal Customs Service], their ability to engage is limited in a number of instances due to the absence of import within the single market of the EAEU."

As a solution to this systemic problem, Vlasta-Consulting proposed creating an operational headquarters under the auspices of the EEC—a Transnational Operational Headquarters (TOSh). Its goal would be to unite the efforts of the customs and law enforcement agencies of the EAEU member states and the private sector to jointly develop tactical solutions.

According to the initiative's concept, the headquarters would be tasked with collecting and analyzing information from all process participants, as well as setting specific tasks for national structures to execute.

"This would make it possible to combine the efforts of both customs authorities, businesses, and the EEC," emphasized Shestera. "To formulate tasks and pass them down for execution to the very same customs services of the EAEU countries, and finally, to set this mechanism in motion, because right now it is at a standstill."
The proposed initiative received lively feedback from forum participants and was recognized as promising for further detailed elaboration with regulators.
subtitle: Representatives of Vlasta-Consulting played a key role in the "Anti-Counterfeit" Forum, proposing an initiative aimed at a systemic solution to the problem of cross-border trafficking of counterfeit products in the countries of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU).

body: The departure of a number of international brands and the suspension of official supply chains have plunged the Russian automotive goods market into a crisis due to a severe shortage of quality materials. According to Izvestia, counterfeit products now outnumber original ones in several categories.

Unscrupulous manufacturers have flooded the market with counterfeit goods, while auto service centers, trying to work with what is available, are often forced to turn away customers or use dubious alternatives, which hits car owners' wallets and compromises their safety.

It is precisely in this challenging environment that our mission is to make a real contribution to legitimizing the market, ensuring quality and safety for consumers. A prime example of this work is a recent joint operation in which specialists from "Vlasta-Consulting" assisted law enforcement agencies—the Main Directorate for Economic Security and Combating Corruption of the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs (GUÉBiPK MVD Russia), the Regional Directorate of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (UMVD), and the Directorate of the Federal Security Service (UFSB) for the Vladimir Region.

In April 2024, a criminal case was initiated for the illegal use of trademarks (Part 3, Article 180 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation). During the investigation, the activities of an illegal workshop in the village of Ileykino were shut down. There, the perpetrators had established a full production cycle: from mixing low-quality base materials to packaging the "products" in canisters copying the packaging of well-known brands, thereby infringing on their rights.

Specialists from "Vlasta-Consulting," engaged as experts, took direct part in the raid. During 22 searches, two production lines, over 25 pallets of finished counterfeit products, packaging materials, and two cargo vehicles used for logistics were discovered and seized. Our key role involved conducting an urgent preliminary examination on-site, which allowed for the immediate identification of the products as counterfeit, proper documentation of all physical evidence, and prevented the perpetrators from covering their tracks.

Additionally, cash amounting to over 2 million rubles was seized from the residences of the individuals involved, along with documentation and electronic media. As a result, five suspects, including the organizer, were detained, and restrictive measures were applied against all of them. Our work does not end here—"Vlasta-Consulting" continues to provide advisory and expert support for the criminal case to fully dismantle the distribution channels and bring the guilty to justice.

Thus, while illegal actors try to profit from the industry's difficult situation, we are making the market fairer, putting a stop to this vicious practice, and protecting those companies that are committed to safeguarding their consumers from substandard products. Our contribution is not just a fight against counterfeiting, but a real step towards cleansing the market and protecting everyone who gets behind the wheel of their car—a clear demonstration of the effectiveness of public-private partnership in the struggle for quality and legality.

body: On July 25, 2025, an important meeting was held at the Federal Customs Service (FCS) of Russia, dedicated to discussing measures to combat the illicit trafficking of tobacco products within the EAEU. The event was chaired by Oleg Galinurovich Gubaidulin, Deputy Head of the FCS.

During the meeting, Oleg Galinurovich expressed readiness to focus on concrete actions and the development of algorithms, while expecting detailed proposals from business representatives on further steps.

One of the key issues raised was the practice of split shipments, a trend involving the use of passenger vehicles instead of cargo trucks. This allows violators to evade sealing requirements and minimize losses in case of vehicle inspections. The problem of split shipments reflects the complex situation in the EAEU market, where goods can quickly move across territories.

Meeting participants emphasized that combating such micro-channels requires gathering information on planned shipments and vehicles used, as well as ensuring rapid response from authorities within 48 hours. Representatives from Vlasta-Consulting expressed readiness to collect data but stressed the need for prompt action, as outdated information significantly reduces the effectiveness of efforts to curb illicit tobacco trafficking.
At the end of the meeting, it was proposed to establish direct 24/7 communication channels with the FCS to enable faster responses to emerging threats.
All participants expressed hope for continued cooperation to achieve stability and legality in the EAEU tobacco market.

body: Shocking Stats: Every Second Part Could Be Fake

A recent investigation by Russia 1 TV revealed that up to 40% of auto parts and motor oils in Russia are counterfeit. Drivers trying to save money end up with fakes—leading to breakdowns, costly repairs, and forced purchases of genuine parts. The result? Double spending and safety risks.
The report emphasized labeling as a way to spot fakes. But the problem runs deeper.
Why Is There So Much Counterfeit Product on the Market?
Experts from Russia 1 TV highlight two major challenges:
• Mixed Shipments: Fakes Hidden Among Genuine Parts
Even trusted suppliers might unknowingly deliver batches contaminated with counterfeits. Blind trust isn’t enough—every part must be checked.
• Marketplaces vs. Repair Shops: Where’s the Risk Higher?
Professional auto services inspect every component before installation. Meanwhile, major online platforms often fail to vet sellers, allowing fakes to be sold as branded goods.
What Does Vlasta-Consulting Propose?
Fighting counterfeits requires more than consumer awareness—it demands market reforms. The solution is a systematic approach.
1.Support for Legal Distributors – Strengthening verification mechanisms, warehouse controls, and supply chain oversight.
2.Cooperation with Regulators – Tighter controls, swift confiscation of counterfeit goods, and suppression of illegal trade.
3.Transparent Supply Chains – From manufacturer to end consumer.
Vlasta-Consulting is committed to making the auto parts market safer.
Choose trusted suppliers. Demand authenticity. Don’t compromise on safety!

excerpt: On July 2, 2025, a meeting of the Customs Regulation Working Group was held at the Eurasian Economic Commission. The event focused on discussing measures to combat illegal nicotine-containing products that are imported and distributed…
body: On July 2, 2025, a meeting of the Customs Regulation Working Group was held at the Eurasian Economic Commission. The event focused on discussing measures to combat illegal nicotine-containing products that are imported and distributed within the EAEU territory.

During the meeting, the current situation on the tobacco product market was analyzed, and proposals from the business community regarding priority customs regulation measures were discussed. Participants examined trends in the illegal circulation of tobacco products and emphasized the importance of preventing unlawful cross-border movement of such goods within the Union.

Special attention was given to navigation seals — a tracking system for monitoring shipments of tobacco and nicotine-containing products. Since January 27, 2025, the use of electronic navigation seals has been mandatory for transporting goods such as alcohol, tobacco products, clothing, footwear, and electronics across the borders of Russia and Belarus. Participants discussed the possibility of expanding their use throughout the Union to enhance control and reduce illegal supplies.
Leaders of Vlasta-Consulting supported the initiatives proposed during the meeting and presented their recommendations for improving the situation in the tobacco market.

At the same time, a growing strategy among violators was described in response to the implementation of navigation seals. The so-called "shipment fragmentation" involves transporting illegal goods in small batches using small vehicles to avoid detection. This tactic complicates efforts to combat illegal tobacco imports.

Representatives of Vlasta expressed their readiness to cooperate with customs authorities and proposed establishing channels for rapid communication and information exchange. This will help respond promptly to violations, especially since routes within the EAEU typically take only a few days to pass.

Vlasta-Consulting will continue participating in discussions on improving customs regulation measures and will carry out informational activities to enhance efforts against illegal products. Engaging in such events allows the company to more effectively represent its clients' interests and contribute to creating transparent business conditions.
subtitle: On July 2, 2025, a meeting of the Customs Regulation Working Group was held at the Eurasian Economic Commission. The event focused on discussing measures to combat illegal nicotine-containing products that are imported and distributed within the EAEU territory.

If a brand is registered only in one of these countries, it significantly complicates full cooperation between customs services and hampers efforts to combat counterfeiting at the international level.

In this regard, the participants urged the business community to register their trademarks in the TRoIS system in both countries. Such an approach will enable Russian and Chinese customs authorities not only to communicate and exchange signals about suspicious shipments but also to take prompt action to prevent them. Ultimately, this will enhance the effectiveness of measures against counterfeit supplies and protect rights holders' interests at the international level.

body: From March 4 to 6, 2025, a large-scale Congress of Leaders of "OPORA RUSSIA" and the Association "NP OPORA" was held in Irkutsk Region, bringing together over 500 participants — representatives of business, federal and regional authorities, financial institutions, and public associations. During the event, eight specialized sessions were conducted, dedicated to the most pressing issues of modern entrepreneurship:
• Foreign economic activity in the face of new challenges;
• Protection of entrepreneurs' rights and legislative improvements;
• Intellectual property and combating patent trolling;
• Support for the defense-industrial complex;
• Implementation of artificial intelligence in manufacturing;
• Effective work with marketplaces and digital platforms.

One of the key sessions was dedicated to "Combating Trolling in Intellectual Property," led by Natalia Zolotykh, Vice President of "OPORA RUSSIA" and Chairperson of the Public Council under Rospatent.
The session addressed urgent questions:
• Who are patent trolls and how do they exploit intellectual property mechanisms?
• Real cases from the alcohol and souvenir industries;
• Effective ways to protect businesses from unscrupulous rights holders.
Experts such as Igor Khavsky (brewery industry) and Grigory Kuzmin (author tourism) provided examples where dishonest rights holders demanded compensation amounts reaching tens of millions of rubles.
Patent attorney Anna Kurapova detailed measures for protection:
• Mandatory patent searches before launching products;
• Registration of trademarks and patents;
• Use of legal mechanisms against abuses.

"Vlasta-Consulting," as an expert in intellectual property protection, supports "OPORA RUSSIA's" position on the necessity of creating a safe business environment where competition is based on principles of fairness and respect for intellectual property.

In the case of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), we believe it is essential to conduct informational work that helps business representatives understand legislative requirements. This will enable them to minimize risks not only related to violations of their IP objects but also to avoid claims from other market participants by developing a competent IP strategy.

Participation in events like the "OPORA RUSSIA" Congress provides an opportunity not only to adopt best practices but also to strengthen partnership ties. body: Employees of the Department of Economic Security and Anti-Corruption of the Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia in the city of Volzhsky, in cooperation with colleagues from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia in Volgograd oblast, detained seven local residents. The director of a commercial organization and his acquaintances are suspected of illegal use of means of individualization of goods committed by an organized group.

It was previously established that illegal activity was carried out on the territory of an industrial enterprise. Along with the production of washing powder of their own registered trademark, the offenders organized the manufacture of household chemicals under the trademarks of a well-known global manufacturer. Counterfeit goods were supplied to several regions of Russia, as well as to one of the neighboring countries.

During searches and inspections of vehicles, the police seized 8.5 thousand packages of washing powder and almost three thousand bottles of detergent with signs of counterfeiting, as well as packaging materials and other items of evidentiary value. body: The specialists of “Vlasta Consulting” ltd conducted the independent research based on the 186 first instance court decisions on the cases of the illegal production, acquisition, storage, transport and sale of the unmarked alcohol and tobacco products is bulk, including the infringement by a group of people by prior conspiracy.

As a result of the work carried out, it was revealed that for the period 2021-2021. only 2.7% of criminal cases (5 decisions) ended with a real term of imprisonment. In the course of the analysis, it was found that most of the court decisions in criminal cases consisted in bringing the infringers to justice by issuing a suspended sentence or paying a fine, fines were also analyzed under Article 171 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, as well as the criminal terms received by the accused. The tobacco industry is one of the most profitable parts of the Russian budget. The illegal market of tobacco products that avoid tax payments, reflects in the shortfalls with the state budget that have the negative impact on the Russian economy in general.

Such insignificant level of the liability and slight punishment for the illegal activity leads to the development of the “shadow” tobacco market. The infringers that are suppressed receive the punishment of the conditional sentence or fine that is much less than their illegal income, that is why the criminals are not afraid of being caught and could continue their illicit activity without any high risks.

Although the LEA officers are actively combating illegal tobacco business and catch the infringers in order to get them to the liability, these suppressed criminals are committed with hardly impunity, as such small court measures do not put enough pressure on the criminal tobacco business.

Taking into account the current situation in Russia with all the sanctions imposed by other countries, there is a 100% possibility of the significant increase of the illegal tobacco market share and the growth of the “underground” producers and illegal distributors of the counterfeit products.

body: Vapes and disposable electric cigarettes as Hqd, izi and others are becoming more and more popular with the teenagers nowadays.  There is a misperception that such devices are harmless in comparison with the ordinary cigarettes and tobacco heating systems. However, it is not true. The production of the disposable electric cigarettes is not legally controlled; thus, the manufacturers could use any kind of poisonous elements in the vape liquids.

Smoking or vaping of such devices negatively impacts the young health of teenagers (target audience of the electric cigarettes) and cause the tense addiction that furtherly results in serious consequences as heart diseases and respiratory infections.

Although the advertising of nicotine products is banned by Instagram, numerous bloggers -idols of the children are showing smoking in their daily “histories” on their social accounts. The teenagers are following this trend of their heroes and want to be like their cult figures from Instagram and Tik-Tok.  Vape-shops are dealing with the famous influencers by purchasing the PR of their electric cigarettes that allows them to place the advertisements on the news feed of millions of teens.  Unlike ordinary cigarettes, these devises are presented for sale online and could be purchased by teenagers.

In the framework of combating these trade, Alexey Solomanidin, executive director of “Vlasta-Consulting” company has shared his opinion on this problem with ‘NTV” channel: “All the commercials and sales of disposable electric cigarettes are aimed at young people. There is no age verification for online sales, thus it is not possible to confirm that the consumer is an adult”. It is a high necessity of developing legal framework to ensure that the sales are not possible for teens as well as implement the sanctions for the violators selling the devises not to adults.

body: As one of the consequences of the pandemic, cybercriminals have begun to actively sell fake doctor’s notes and vaccination certificates. As an experiment, the Russia-24 channel’s film crew asked for such a service and made an appointment with the courier to receive a certificate confirming vaccination against COVID-19. The certificate purchased under a fictitious name was delivered by a courier, and later, upon examining the document, they found that the certificate was made in high quality (glossy paper, clear print, clinic stamps and doctor's signature). It was discovered that the doctor who signed the certificate actually works in this medical institution. In this regard, a visit was made to the polyclinic, where the head doctor did not want to talk and answer questions. This indicates the consistency and interest of all parties in these violations.

Konstantin Shestera, operating director of the consulting company Vlasta-Consulting: “It can be argued that the certificate was actually issued in a medical institution, whose stamp is on it, but this does not negate the fact that the document is fake, since the person who received this certificate has not been vaccinated. " Buyers of these certificates naively believe that by purchasing such documents, they will be able to receive real protection and safely leave the country, but this is a delusion. The best confirmation is an electronic certificate of completion of the second stage of vaccination, upon which the data of the vaccinated patient is entered into the database of the medical organization and into the unified medical information and analytical system. In addition, police officers do not stop searching the Internet for organizations offering illegal services. Indeed, with a thorough check, fake certificates and certificates are easily recognized, and for the use of such a "meaningless piece of paper" you might end up paying with your own freedom.

Alexey Solomanidin, executive director of the consulting company Vlasta-Consulting: “This is a matter of criminal liability and risks not only for the seller and manufacturer, but also for the buyer and the bearer of this certificate. The punishments under this article are quite serious, up to and including imprisonment. " In addition to the original document on vaccination, this procedure provides protection against a dangerous virus, and this is currently of crucial importance.

Illegal cigarettes can be contraband or counterfeit. The former is usually smuggled across the border, and representatives of the FCS are called upon to fight against this. After explaining the whole situation, he decided to independently and promptly destroy the goods he had brought. Konstantin Shestera, Deputy General Director of Vlasta-Consulting, reviewed two brands of BT and Dubao cigarettes, which should not technically be on sale. body: On January 1, a legal provision aimed at combating the harmful effects of nicotine came into force in Russia. Now, more than one block of unmarked packs of cigarettes cannot be transported across the country, that is, without Russian excise stamps.

There is no limit to the ingenuity of tobacco smugglers. Illegal cigarettes are imported into Russia in hiding places, under the dashboard and on fake invoices - even under the guise of oat bran. As soon as the cigarettes cross the border, it is more difficult to stop the smuggling further.

Alexey Solomanidin, executive director of Vlasta-Consulting consulting company, stated: “Police officers, stopping a car full of illegal cigarettes, are told that they are intended for personal use, and under current law the officers cannot do anything, because either they need to escort the car to the warehouse and prove the fact of sale, or just let it go "
The State Duma generally believes that many tobacco producers in the neighboring countries work specifically for the illegal market in Russia.

Sergey Katasonov, deputy of the State Duma of the Russian Federation, stated: “In Belarus the excise tax is five times lower than that of Russia, but the capacities of their factories exceed the internal demand by 5 times. It is clear that they work for our market."

On January 1, 2021, a law came into force limiting the transportation of more than 200 unmarked cigarettes across the country, that is, purchased abroad, in the same hands. The ban does not apply to legal cigarettes.

Sergey Katasonov, deputy of the State Duma of the Russian Federation, stated: “To say that this will be a drastic change for Russians is wrong. It's just that now, when you come from Armenia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, you should keep in mind that there is a standard for the import of unmarked tobacco products. "

The problem is that this is a law without implementation: there is a ban, but there is no punishment. However, the State Duma intends to fix this in a couple of months. The project in progress suggests a fine of up to 50 thousand rubles (675 USD). The police will issue the protocols. This will become the case when smoking is expensive not just figuratively, but quite literally.
subtitle: On January 1, a legal provision aimed at combating the harmful effects of nicotine came into force in Russia. Now, more than one block of unmarked packs of cigarettes cannot be transported across the country, that is, without Russian excise stamps.

body: It is common to find counterfeit on the shelves under the guise of imported cigarettes. Moreover, such an "elite" pack can cost an exorbitant price. But the cost can only be explained by the greed of the sellers, and the smoker risks paying twice. This illusion of saving money comes at the cost of one's own health. COVID-19 has also contributed to this problem, since the trade in low-grade tobacco now takes place via the Internet and courier delivery. Duplicates and fakes are openly traded on websites, often without making any attempt to hide it.

Moscow Patrol, together with the employees of Vlasta-Consulting company, who specialize in detecting counterfeits, ordered tobacco products through an online store and analyzed the samples obtained. Konstantin Shestera, head of the anti-counterfeiting department of the consulting company Vlasta Consulting, made the following conclusion: “The quality of the purchased pack of cigarettes is very low, and the excise stamps do not have the necessary elements that should be displayed in ultraviolet light. title: Only tightening the law will help to defeat counterfeit in Russia
h1: Only tightening the law will help to defeat counterfeit in Russia
metaTitle: Only tightening the law will help to defeat counterfeit in Russia

excerpt: In Russia, violators in case of administrative punishment can face a fine of 10 thousand rubles, and only in case of criminal liability, the term of imprisonment can be up to 6 years. But the law enforcement practice is such that it is…
body: In Russia, violators in case of administrative punishment can face a fine of 10 thousand rubles, and only in case of criminal liability, the term of imprisonment can be up to 6 years. But the law enforcement practice is such that it is extremely difficult to get criminal punishment.

Only in order to initiate a criminal case, the police need to prove that the damage was at least 250 thousand rubles and that the crime was committed intentionally, and even to identify all possible affiliates and parties

If in Moscow the Department for Combating Economic Crimes still somehow copes with the load, then in the regions manufacturers and sellers of fakes can feel completely safe. The same seller can be caught multiple times in the same crime - and still pay the same small fines if he uses different legal entities.

There are counterfeit products in all product groups. According to the Ministry of Economic Development of the Russian Federation, half of the auto parts on the Russian market are fakes, and this is more than 700 billion rubles a year. The turnover of illegal tobacco, according to Vlasta-Consulting, is estimated at more than 100 billion rubles a year. The budgets of all levels are losing hundreds of billions of rubles. But the bigger problem is that these products are dangerous. Surrogate alcohol with methanol, counterfeit, dummy drugs, fake airbags, counterfeit cigarettes - all this takes the lives of thousands of people.

Channels for counterfeiting to the Russian market are also not a secret. The common customs area of the Eurasian Union allows any volume of products from China to be imported to Russia through Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan almost without hindrance. According to the Ministry of Industry and Trade, the volume of unrecorded imports of clothing and footwear in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan exceeds $ 5 billion a year, which is many times higher than the demand in these countries.

Digitalization of trade poses a serious risk of further growth of counterfeit products. In 2019, more than half a million online sources for the sale of counterfeits were closed. For example, it is extremely difficult to close public pages in social messengers due to the presence of many “reserve” groups. Counterfeit goods also end up on large marketplaces: the goods there are often sold not by the portal itself, but by some of the partners, and of course, the authenticity assessment is not carried out.

There are a lot of videos on the Web about how to sell goods from the wholesale and retail markets on marketplaces. At the same time, marketplaces act only as an agent between the client and the supplier. It is very difficult to bring such platforms to justice at the moment due to the peculiarities of the current legislation.

Law enforcement practice shows that the liberalization of the Criminal Code de facto deprived the police of the opportunity to fight counterfeit. And during the upcoming session of the State Duma, it is necessary to raise the issue of tightening it. Of course, we will not be ahead of China in the world ranking of leaders in counterfeit trafficking, but letting the situation take its course, the “honorable” second place for our country will remain for a long time.
subtitle: In Russia, violators in case of administrative punishment can face a fine of 10 thousand rubles, and only in case of criminal liability, the term of imprisonment can be up to 6 years.

body: One of the WABCO partners encountered an obvious defect. The audit began with a test purchase, and unfortunately for counterfeiters, the WABCO partner specializes in information and legal services. The fraudsters thought they acted sly. They made fake desiccants, but they screwed the original cartridge onto them. That is, the consumer had no doubts, if only there was more than one subtlety: the method of applying the WABCO logo to the casting. It is on these nuances that manufacturers of fakes usually stumble, along with knowing little about the policies that manufacturing firms are pursuing. So, for consumer protection in 2015, WABCO registered a trademark at the customs of the Russian Federation. And since then, no one, with the exception of a number of authorized companies, can import products into the territory of the Russian Federation. To help customers easily identify original spare parts, WABCO has developed new special packaging. Thanks to WABCO's distinctive PrioSpot® code and the ability to use a simple online tool to check a unique serial number, the consumer can always be sure that they are using an original WABCO product. At the same time, with the new range of budgetary ProVia parts, alternatives have been offered specifically designed for used vehicles. These measures made it possible in September 2018 to identify a large batch of counterfeit air dryer cartridges in the Volga Federal District.   The lucrative business was suppressed with the police in November last year in the trade facility "Avtomag-NN" LLC in Nizhny Novgorod on Fuchik Street, 38. It turned out to be a rich catch: one and a half hundred filters, taps and dryer kits, 33 repair kits in cardboard boxes and plastic bags, ABS system modulators. All products were marked with the WABCO trademark. The total prevented damage amounted to almost 2 million rubles. ... On February 27, 2019, the lawyers of Vlasta-Consulting LLC, on behalf of WABCO, supported the demands of the police to bring violators to justice. The proceedings in the case of illegal use of means of individualization of goods ended on March 4, 2019. Avtomag-NN LLC was brought to administrative responsibility under Part 2 of Art. 14.10. "Illegal use of means of individualization of goods." The punishment was a fine of 100,000 rubles and the confiscation of all counterfeit products. The Arbitration Court decision of the Nizhny Novgorod Region was made in full on March 4, 2019. The entrepreneurs did not use the opportunity to appeal, which expired on March 19, 2019.

body: Law enforcement agencies have discovered and closed the illegal production of motor oils in Moscow and Moscow region, according to the website of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. According to preliminary estimates, the criminals' income was about 1 billion rubles a month. Motor oils that did not meet the requirements of technical regulations were produced on an industrial scale in the capital and in the Solnechnogorsk district of Moscow region. The workers were mostly immigrants from the countries of Central Asia. The finished products were sold under the brands of well-known world manufacturers in all regions of the country.   Employees of the Anti-Corruption Department, with the support of riot policemen, conducted 16 searches in the premises of production, storage and sale of counterfeit goods, as well as in the offices and places of residence of the persons involved in the case. The raids uncovered 3 automated lines for bottling and packaging of motor oil, more than 70 tons of petroleum products, over 80 thousand packages of ready-to-sell products, large quantities of branded plastic containers and labels of various brands, as well as accounting documents and seals of more than 30 legal entities. The removal of the seized products took place over several weeks. On the basis of the collected materials against the members of the group, the Main Investigation Department of the Main Directorate of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia for the Moscow Region opened a criminal case on the grounds of a crime under Part 3 of Art. 180 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation "Illegal use of means of individualization of goods, committed by an organized group."
